 232 │ def parse_tag(
 233 │     tag: str, *, validate_order: bool = False, limit: int | None = None
 234 │ ) -> frozenset[Tag]:
 235 │     """
 236 │     Parses the provided tag (e.g. `py3-none-any`) into a frozenset of
 237 │     :class:`Tag` instances.
 238 │ 
 239 │     Returning a set is required due to the possibility that the tag is a
 240 │     `compressed tag set`_, e.g. ``"py2.py3-none-any"`` which supports both
 241 │     Python 2 and Python 3.
 242 │ 
 243 │     If **validate_order** is true, compressed tag set components are checked
 244 │     to be in sorted order as required by PEP 425.
 245 │ 
 246 │     If **limit** is not ``None``, the compressed tag set can generate at most
 247 │     that many tags.
 248 │ 
 249 │     :param str tag: The tag to parse, e.g. ``"py3-none-any"``.
 250 │     :param bool validate_order: Check whether compressed tag set components
 251 │         are in sorted order.
 252 │     :param int | None limit: The maximum number of tags to parse.
 253 │     :raises UnsortedTagsError: If **validate_order** is true and any compressed tag
 254 │         set component is not in sorted order.
 255 │     :raises InvalidTag: If the interpreter field is not an identifier; if the
 256 │         interpreter, ABI, or platform field (or any member of a compressed tag
 257 │         set) is empty; or if the tag does not have exactly three components.
 258 │     :raises TooManyTagsError: If **limit** is not ``None`` and the compressed tag
 259 │         set would generate more than **limit** tags.
 260 │     :raises ValueError: If **limit** is negative.
 261 │ 
 262 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
 263 │        The *validate_order* parameter.
 264 │ 
 265 │     .. versionadded:: 26.3
 266 │        Raises :class:`InvalidTag` when an interpreter component is not an
 267 │        identifier, a tag component is empty, or a tag does not have exactly
 268 │        three components.
 269 │        Added the *limit* parameter. Raises :class:`TooManyTagsError` if the compressed
 270 │        tag set would generate more than *limit* tags.
 271 │     """
 272 │ 
 273 │     if limit is not None and limit < 0:
 274 │         raise ValueError("limit must be non-negative")
 275 │ 
 276 │     component_parts = [component.split(".") for component in tag.split("-")]
 277 │     for parts in component_parts:
 278 │         if "" in parts:
 279 │             component = ".".join(parts)
 280 │             raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} has an empty component: {component!r}")
 281 │         if validate_order and parts != sorted(parts):
 282 │             component = ".".join(parts)
 283 │             raise UnsortedTagsError(
 284 │                 f"Tag component {component!r} is not in sorted order per PEP 425"
 285 │             )
 286 │ 
 287 │     tag_count = 1
 288 │     for parts in component_parts:
 289 │         tag_count *= len(parts)
 290 │ 
 291 │     if limit is not None and tag_count > limit:
 292 │         raise TooManyTagsError(
 293 │             f"Compressed tag set would generate {tag_count} tags, exceeding "
 294 │             f"limit {limit}"
 295 │         )
 296 │ 
 297 │     try:
 298 │         interpreters, abis, platforms = component_parts
 299 │     except ValueError as exc:
 300 │         raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} must have exactly three components") from exc
 301 │     for interpreter in interpreters:
 302 │         if not interpreter.isidentifier():
 303 │             raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} has an invalid interpreter: {interpreter!r}")
 304 │     return frozenset(
 305 │         Tag(interpreter, abi, platform_)
 306 │         for interpreter in interpreters
 307 │         for abi in abis
 308 │         for platform_ in platforms
 309 │     )

 364 │ def _cpython_abis(py_version: PythonVersion, warn: bool = False) -> list[str]:
 365 │     py_version = tuple(py_version)  # To allow for version comparison.
 366 │     abis = []
 367 │     version = _version_nodot(py_version[:2])
 368 │     threading = debug = pymalloc = ucs4 = ""
 369 │     with_debug = _get_config_var("Py_DEBUG", warn)
 370 │     has_refcount = hasattr(sys, "gettotalrefcount")
 371 │     # Windows doesn't set Py_DEBUG, so checking for support of debug-compiled
 372 │     # extension modules is the best option.
 373 │     # https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/3383#issuecomment-173267692
 374 │     has_ext = "_d.pyd" in EXTENSION_SUFFIXES
 375 │     if with_debug or (with_debug is None and (has_refcount or has_ext)):
 376 │         debug = "d"
 377 │     if py_version >= (3, 13) and _get_config_var("Py_GIL_DISABLED", warn):
 378 │         threading = "t"
 379 │     if py_version < (3, 8):
 380 │         with_pymalloc = _get_config_var("WITH_PYMALLOC", warn)
 381 │         if with_pymalloc or with_pymalloc is None:
 382 │             pymalloc = "m"
 383 │         if py_version < (3, 3):
 384 │             unicode_size = _get_config_var("Py_UNICODE_SIZE", warn)
 385 │             if unicode_size == 4 or (
 386 │                 unicode_size is None and sys.maxunicode == 0x10FFFF
 387 │             ):
 388 │                 ucs4 = "u"
 389 │     elif debug:
 390 │         # Debug builds can also load "normal" extension modules.
 391 │         # We can also assume no UCS-4 or pymalloc requirement.
 392 │         abis.append(f"cp{version}{threading}")
 393 │     abis.insert(0, f"cp{version}{threading}{debug}{pymalloc}{ucs4}")
 394 │     return abis

 397 │ def cpython_tags(
 398 │     python_version: PythonVersion | None = None,
 399 │     abis: Iterable[str] | None = None,
 400 │     platforms: Iterable[str] | None = None,
 401 │     *,
 402 │     warn: bool = False,
 403 │ ) -> Iterator[Tag]:
 404 │     """
 405 │     Yields the tags for the CPython interpreter.
 406 │ 
 407 │     The specific tags generated are:
 408 │ 
 409 │     - ``cp<python_version>-<abi>-<platform>``
 410 │     - ``cp<python_version>-<stable_abi>-<platform>``
 411 │     - ``cp<python_version>-none-<platform>``
 412 │     - ``cp<older version>-<stable_abi>-<platform>`` where "older version" is all older
 413 │       minor versions down to Python 3.2 (when ``abi3`` was introduced)
 414 │ 
 415 │     If ``python_version`` only provides a major-only version then only
 416 │     user-provided ABIs via ``abis`` and the ``none`` ABI will be used.
 417 │ 
 418 │     The ``stable_abi`` will be either ``abi3`` or ``abi3t`` if `abi` is a
 419 │     GIL-enabled ABI like `"cp315"` or a free-threaded ABI like `"cp315t"`,
 420 │     respectively.
 421 │ 
 422 │     :param Sequence python_version: A one- or two-item sequence representing the
 423 │                                  targeted Python version. Defaults to
 424 │                                  ``sys.version_info[:2]``.
 425 │     :param Iterable abis: Iterable of compatible ABIs. Defaults to the ABIs
 426 │                           compatible with the current system.
 427 │     :param Iterable platforms: Iterable of compatible platforms. Defaults to the
 428 │                                platforms compatible with the current system.
 429 │     :param bool warn: Whether warnings should be logged. Defaults to ``False``.
 430 │ 
 431 │     .. versionadded:: 20.0
 432 │     """
 433 │     if not python_version:
 434 │         python_version = sys.version_info[:2]
 435 │ 
 436 │     interpreter = f"cp{_version_nodot(python_version[:2])}"
 437 │ 
 438 │     if abis is None:
 439 │         abis = _cpython_abis(python_version, warn) if len(python_version) > 1 else []
 440 │     abis = list(abis)
 441 │     threading = _is_threaded_cpython(abis)
 442 │     # Stable ABIs and 'none' are explicitly handled later.
 443 │     explicit_abis = ("abi3", "abi3t", "none") if threading else ("abi3", "none")
 444 │     for explicit_abi in explicit_abis:
 445 │         try:
 446 │             abis.remove(explicit_abi)
 447 │         except ValueError:  # noqa: PERF203
 448 │             pass
 449 │ 
 450 │     platforms = list(platforms or platform_tags())
 451 │     for abi in abis:
 452 │         for platform_ in platforms:
 453 │             yield Tag(interpreter, abi, platform_)
 454 │ 
 455 │     use_abi3 = _abi3_applies(python_version, threading)
 456 │     use_abi3t = _abi3t_applies(python_version, threading)
 457 │     if use_abi3:
 458 │         yield from (Tag(interpreter, "abi3", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 459 │     if use_abi3t:
 460 │         yield from (Tag(interpreter, "abi3t", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 461 │ 
 462 │     yield from (Tag(interpreter, "none", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 463 │ 
 464 │     if use_abi3 or use_abi3t:
 465 │         for minor_version in range(python_version[1] - 1, 1, -1):
 466 │             for platform_ in platforms:
 467 │                 version = _version_nodot((python_version[0], minor_version))
 468 │                 interpreter = f"cp{version}"
 469 │                 if use_abi3:
 470 │                     yield Tag(interpreter, "abi3", platform_)
 471 │                 if use_abi3t:
 472 │                     # Support for abi3t was introduced in Python 3.15, but in
 473 │                     # principle abi3t wheels are possible for older limited API
 474 │                     # versions, so allow things like ("cp37", "abi3t", "platform")
 475 │                     yield Tag(interpreter, "abi3t", platform_)

 478 │ def _generic_abi() -> list[str]:
 479 │     """
 480 │     Return the ABI tag based on EXT_SUFFIX.
 481 │     """
 482 │     # The following are examples of `EXT_SUFFIX`.
 483 │     # We want to keep the parts which are related to the ABI and remove the
 484 │     # parts which are related to the platform:
 485 │     # - linux:   '.cpython-310-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' => cp310
 486 │     # - mac:     '.cpython-310-darwin.so'           => cp310
 487 │     # - win:     '.cp310-win_amd64.pyd'             => cp310
 488 │     # - win:     '.pyd'                             => cp37 (uses _cpython_abis())
 489 │     # - pypy:    '.pypy38-pp73-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' => pypy38_pp73
 490 │     # - graalpy: '.graalpy-38-native-x86_64-darwin.dylib'
 491 │     #                                               => graalpy_38_native
 492 │ 
 493 │     ext_suffix = _get_config_var("EXT_SUFFIX", warn=True)
 494 │     if not isinstance(ext_suffix, str) or not ext_suffix.startswith("."):
 495 │         raise SystemError("invalid sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')")
 496 │     parts = ext_suffix.split(".")
 497 │     if len(parts) < 3:
 498 │         # CPython3.7 and earlier uses ".pyd" on Windows.
 499 │         return _cpython_abis(sys.version_info[:2])
 500 │     soabi = parts[1]
 501 │     if soabi.startswith("cpython"):
 502 │         # non-windows
 503 │         cpython_parts = soabi.split("-")
 504 │         if len(cpython_parts) < 2 or not cpython_parts[1]:
 505 │             raise SystemError("invalid sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')")
 506 │         abi = "cp" + cpython_parts[1]
 507 │     elif soabi.startswith("cp"):
 508 │         # windows
 509 │         abi = soabi.split("-")[0]
 510 │     elif soabi.startswith("pypy"):
 511 │         abi = "-".join(soabi.split("-")[:2])
 512 │     elif soabi.startswith("graalpy"):
 513 │         abi = "-".join(soabi.split("-")[:3])
 514 │     elif soabi:
 515 │         # pyston, ironpython, others?
 516 │         abi = soabi
 517 │     else:
 518 │         return []
 519 │     return [_normalize_string(abi)]

 165 │ 
 166 │     @property
 167 │     def abi(self) -> str:
 168 │         """
 169 │         The supported ABI.
 170 │         """
 171 │         return self._abi
 172 │ 
 173 │     @property
 174 │     def platform(self) -> str:
 175 │         """
 176 │         The OS/platform.
 177 │         """
 178 │         return self._platform
 179 │ 
 180 │     def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
 181 │         if not isinstance(other, Tag):
 182 │             return NotImplemented
 183 │ 
 184 │         return (
 185 │             (self._hash == other._hash)  # Short-circuit ASAP for perf reasons.
 186 │             and (self._platform == other._platform)
 187 │             and (self._abi == other._abi)
 188 │             and (self._interpreter == other._interpreter)
 189 │         )
 190 │ 
 191 │     def __hash__(self) -> int:
 192 │         return self._hash
 193 │ 
 194 │     def __str__(self) -> str:
 195 │         return f"{self._interpreter}-{self._abi}-{self._platform}"
 196 │ 
 197 │     def __repr__(self) -> str:
 198 │         return f"<{self} @ {id(self)}>"
 199 │ 
 200 │     def __getstate__(self) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
 201 │         # Return state as a 3-item tuple: (interpreter, abi, platform).
 202 │         # Cache member _hash is excluded and will be recomputed.
 203 │         return (self._interpreter, self._abi, self._platform)
 204 │ 
 205 │     def __setstate__(self, state: object) -> None:
 206 │         if isinstance(state, tuple):
 207 │             if len(state) == 3 and all(isinstance(s, str) for s in state):
 208 │                 # New format (26.2+): (interpreter, abi, platform)
 209 │                 self._interpreter, self._abi, self._platform = state
 210 │                 self._hash = hash((self._interpreter, self._abi, self._platform))
 211 │                 return
 212 │             if len(state) == 2 and isinstance(state[1], dict):
 213 │                 # Old format (packaging <= 26.1, __slots__): (None, {slot: value}).
 214 │                 _, slots = state
 215 │                 try:
 216 │                     interpreter = slots["_interpreter"]
 217 │                     abi = slots["_abi"]
 218 │                     platform = slots["_platform"]
 219 │                 except KeyError:
 220 │                     raise TypeError(f"Cannot restore Tag from {state!r}") from None
 221 │                 if not all(
 222 │                     isinstance(value, str) for value in (interpreter, abi, platform)
 223 │                 ):
 224 │                     raise TypeError(f"Cannot restore Tag from {state!r}")
 225 │                 self._interpreter = interpreter.lower()
 226 │                 self._abi = abi.lower()
 227 │                 self._platform = platform.lower()
 228 │                 self._hash = hash((self._interpreter, self._abi, self._platform))
 229 │                 return
 230 │         raise TypeError(f"Cannot restore Tag from {state!r}")

 233 │ def parse_tag(
 234 │     tag: str, *, validate_order: bool = False, limit: int | None = None
 235 │ ) -> frozenset[Tag]:
 236 │     """
 237 │     Parses the provided tag (e.g. `py3-none-any`) into a frozenset of
 238 │     :class:`Tag` instances.
 239 │ 
 240 │     Returning a set is required due to the possibility that the tag is a
 241 │     `compressed tag set`_, e.g. ``"py2.py3-none-any"`` which supports both
 242 │     Python 2 and Python 3.
 243 │ 
 244 │     If **validate_order** is true, compressed tag set components are checked
 245 │     to be in sorted order as required by PEP 425.
 246 │ 
 247 │     If **limit** is not ``None``, the compressed tag set can generate at most
 248 │     that many tags.
 249 │ 
 250 │     :param str tag: The tag to parse, e.g. ``"py3-none-any"``.
 251 │     :param bool validate_order: Check whether compressed tag set components
 252 │         are in sorted order.
 253 │     :param int | None limit: The maximum number of tags to parse.
 254 │     :raises UnsortedTagsError: If **validate_order** is true and any compressed tag
 255 │         set component is not in sorted order.
 256 │     :raises InvalidTag: If the interpreter field is not an identifier; if the
 257 │         interpreter, ABI, or platform field (or any member of a compressed tag
 258 │         set) is empty; or if the tag does not have exactly three components.
 259 │     :raises TooManyTagsError: If **limit** is not ``None`` and the compressed tag
 260 │         set would generate more than **limit** tags.
 261 │     :raises ValueError: If **limit** is negative.
 262 │ 
 263 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
 264 │        The *validate_order* parameter.
 265 │ 
 266 │     .. versionadded:: 26.3
 267 │        Raises :class:`InvalidTag` when an interpreter component is not an
 268 │        identifier, a tag component is empty, or a tag does not have exactly
 269 │        three components.
 270 │        Added the *limit* parameter. Raises :class:`TooManyTagsError` if the compressed
 271 │        tag set would generate more than *limit* tags.
 272 │     """
 273 │ 
 274 │     if limit is not None and limit < 0:
 275 │         raise ValueError("limit must be non-negative")
 276 │ 
 277 │     component_parts = [component.split(".") for component in tag.split("-")]
 278 │     for parts in component_parts:
 279 │         if "" in parts:
 280 │             component = ".".join(parts)
 281 │             raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} has an empty component: {component!r}")
 282 │         if validate_order and parts != sorted(parts):
 283 │             component = ".".join(parts)
 284 │             raise UnsortedTagsError(
 285 │                 f"Tag component {component!r} is not in sorted order per PEP 425"
 286 │             )
 287 │ 
 288 │     tag_count = 1
 289 │     for parts in component_parts:
 290 │         tag_count *= len(parts)
 291 │ 
 292 │     if limit is not None and tag_count > limit:
 293 │         raise TooManyTagsError(
 294 │             f"Compressed tag set would generate {tag_count} tags, exceeding "
 295 │             f"limit {limit}"
 296 │         )
 297 │ 
 298 │     try:
 299 │         interpreters, abis, platforms = component_parts
 300 │     except ValueError as exc:
 301 │         raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} must have exactly three components") from exc
 302 │     for interpreter in interpreters:
 303 │         if not interpreter.isidentifier():
 304 │             raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} has an invalid interpreter: {interpreter!r}")
 305 │     return frozenset(
 306 │         Tag(interpreter, abi, platform_)
 307 │         for interpreter in interpreters
 308 │         for abi in abis
 309 │         for platform_ in platforms
 310 │     )

 326 │ def _is_threaded_cpython(abis: list[str]) -> bool:
 327 │     """
 328 │     Determine if the ABI corresponds to a threaded (`--disable-gil`) build.
 329 │ 
 330 │     The threaded builds are indicated by a "t" in the abiflags.
 331 │     """
 332 │     if len(abis) == 0:
 333 │         return False
 334 │     # expect e.g., cp313
 335 │     m = re.match(r"cp\d+(.*)", abis[0])
 336 │     if not m:
 337 │         return False
 338 │     abiflags = m.group(1)

 347 │     builds do not support abi3.

 357 │     returns tags going back to Python 3.2 to mirror the abi3
 358 │     implementation and leave open the possibility of abi3t wheels

 365 │ def _cpython_abis(py_version: PythonVersion, warn: bool = False) -> list[str]:
 366 │     py_version = tuple(py_version)  # To allow for version comparison.
 367 │     abis = []
 368 │     version = _version_nodot(py_version[:2])
 369 │     threading = debug = pymalloc = ucs4 = ""
 370 │     with_debug = _get_config_var("Py_DEBUG", warn)
 371 │     has_refcount = hasattr(sys, "gettotalrefcount")
 372 │     # Windows doesn't set Py_DEBUG, so checking for support of debug-compiled
 373 │     # extension modules is the best option.
 374 │     # https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/3383#issuecomment-173267692
 375 │     has_ext = "_d.pyd" in EXTENSION_SUFFIXES
 376 │     if with_debug or (with_debug is None and (has_refcount or has_ext)):
 377 │         debug = "d"
 378 │     if py_version >= (3, 13) and _get_config_var("Py_GIL_DISABLED", warn):
 379 │         threading = "t"
 380 │     if py_version < (3, 8):
 381 │         with_pymalloc = _get_config_var("WITH_PYMALLOC", warn)
 382 │         if with_pymalloc or with_pymalloc is None:
 383 │             pymalloc = "m"
 384 │         if py_version < (3, 3):
 385 │             unicode_size = _get_config_var("Py_UNICODE_SIZE", warn)
 386 │             if unicode_size == 4 or (
 387 │                 unicode_size is None and sys.maxunicode == 0x10FFFF
 388 │             ):
 389 │                 ucs4 = "u"
 390 │     elif debug:
 391 │         # Debug builds can also load "normal" extension modules.
 392 │         # We can also assume no UCS-4 or pymalloc requirement.
 393 │         abis.append(f"cp{version}{threading}")
 394 │     abis.insert(0, f"cp{version}{threading}{debug}{pymalloc}{ucs4}")
 395 │     return abis

 398 │ def cpython_tags(
 399 │     python_version: PythonVersion | None = None,
 400 │     abis: Iterable[str] | None = None,
 401 │     platforms: Iterable[str] | None = None,
 402 │     *,
 403 │     warn: bool = False,
 404 │ ) -> Iterator[Tag]:
 405 │     """
 406 │     Yields the tags for the CPython interpreter.
 407 │ 
 408 │     The specific tags generated are:
 409 │ 
 410 │     - ``cp<python_version>-<abi>-<platform>``
 411 │     - ``cp<python_version>-<stable_abi>-<platform>``
 412 │     - ``cp<python_version>-none-<platform>``
 413 │     - ``cp<older version>-<stable_abi>-<platform>`` where "older version" is all older
 414 │       minor versions down to Python 3.2 (when ``abi3`` was introduced)
 415 │ 
 416 │     If ``python_version`` only provides a major-only version then only
 417 │     user-provided ABIs via ``abis`` and the ``none`` ABI will be used.
 418 │ 
 419 │     The ``stable_abi`` will be either ``abi3`` or ``abi3t`` if `abi` is a
 420 │     GIL-enabled ABI like `"cp315"` or a free-threaded ABI like `"cp315t"`,
 421 │     respectively.
 422 │ 
 423 │     :param Sequence python_version: A one- or two-item sequence representing the
 424 │                                  targeted Python version. Defaults to
 425 │                                  ``sys.version_info[:2]``.
 426 │     :param Iterable abis: Iterable of compatible ABIs. Defaults to the ABIs
 427 │                           compatible with the current system.
 428 │     :param Iterable platforms: Iterable of compatible platforms. Defaults to the
 429 │                                platforms compatible with the current system.
 430 │     :param bool warn: Whether warnings should be logged. Defaults to ``False``.
 431 │ 
 432 │     .. versionadded:: 20.0
 433 │     """
 434 │     if not python_version:
 435 │         python_version = sys.version_info[:2]
 436 │ 
 437 │     interpreter = f"cp{_version_nodot(python_version[:2])}"
 438 │ 
 439 │     if abis is None:
 440 │         abis = _cpython_abis(python_version, warn) if len(python_version) > 1 else []
 441 │     abis = list(abis)
 442 │     threading = _is_threaded_cpython(abis)
 443 │     # Stable ABIs and 'none' are explicitly handled later.
 444 │     explicit_abis = ("abi3", "abi3t", "none") if threading else ("abi3", "none")
 445 │     for explicit_abi in explicit_abis:
 446 │         try:
 447 │             abis.remove(explicit_abi)
 448 │         except ValueError:  # noqa: PERF203
 449 │             pass
 450 │ 
 451 │     platforms = list(platforms or platform_tags())
 452 │     for abi in abis:
 453 │         for platform_ in platforms:
 454 │             yield Tag(interpreter, abi, platform_)
 455 │ 
 456 │     use_abi3 = _abi3_applies(python_version, threading)
 457 │     use_abi3t = _abi3t_applies(python_version, threading)
 458 │     if use_abi3:
 459 │         yield from (Tag(interpreter, "abi3", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 460 │     if use_abi3t:
 461 │         yield from (Tag(interpreter, "abi3t", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 462 │ 
 463 │     yield from (Tag(interpreter, "none", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 464 │ 
 465 │     if use_abi3 or use_abi3t:
 466 │         for minor_version in range(python_version[1] - 1, 1, -1):
 467 │             for platform_ in platforms:
 468 │                 version = _version_nodot((python_version[0], minor_version))
 469 │                 interpreter = f"cp{version}"
 470 │                 if use_abi3:
 471 │                     yield Tag(interpreter, "abi3", platform_)
 472 │                 if use_abi3t:
 473 │                     # Support for abi3t was introduced in Python 3.15, but in
 474 │                     # principle abi3t wheels are possible for older limited API
 475 │                     # versions, so allow things like ("cp37", "abi3t", "platform")
 476 │                     yield Tag(interpreter, "abi3t", platform_)
 477 │

 479 │ def _generic_abi() -> list[str]:
 480 │     """
 481 │     Return the ABI tag based on EXT_SUFFIX.
 482 │     """
 483 │     # The following are examples of `EXT_SUFFIX`.
 484 │     # We want to keep the parts which are related to the ABI and remove the
 485 │     # parts which are related to the platform:
 486 │     # - linux:   '.cpython-310-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' => cp310
 487 │     # - mac:     '.cpython-310-darwin.so'           => cp310
 488 │     # - win:     '.cp310-win_amd64.pyd'             => cp310
 489 │     # - win:     '.pyd'                             => cp37 (uses _cpython_abis())
 490 │     # - pypy:    '.pypy38-pp73-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' => pypy38_pp73
 491 │     # - graalpy: '.graalpy-38-native-x86_64-darwin.dylib'
 492 │     #                                               => graalpy_38_native
 493 │ 
 494 │     ext_suffix = _get_config_var("EXT_SUFFIX", warn=True)
 495 │     if not isinstance(ext_suffix, str) or not ext_suffix.startswith("."):
 496 │         raise SystemError("invalid sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')")
 497 │     parts = ext_suffix.split(".")
 498 │     if len(parts) < 3:
 499 │         # CPython3.7 and earlier uses ".pyd" on Windows.
 500 │         return _cpython_abis(sys.version_info[:2])
 501 │     soabi = parts[1]
 502 │     if soabi.startswith("cpython"):
 503 │         # non-windows
 504 │         cpython_parts = soabi.split("-")
 505 │         if len(cpython_parts) < 2 or not cpython_parts[1]:
 506 │             raise SystemError("invalid sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')")
 507 │         abi = "cp" + cpython_parts[1]
 508 │     elif soabi.startswith("cp"):
 509 │         # windows
 510 │         abi = soabi.split("-")[0]
 511 │     elif soabi.startswith("pypy"):
 512 │         abi = "-".join(soabi.split("-")[:2])
 513 │     elif soabi.startswith("graalpy"):
 514 │         abi = "-".join(soabi.split("-")[:3])
 515 │     elif soabi:
 516 │         # pyston, ironpython, others?
 517 │         abi = soabi
 518 │     else:
 519 │         return []
 520 │     return [_normalize_string(abi)]

 683 │ def mac_platforms(
 684 │     version: AppleVersion | None = None, arch: str | None = None
 685 │ ) -> Iterator[str]:
 686 │     """
 687 │     Yields the :attr:`~Tag.platform` tags for macOS.
 688 │ 
 689 │     The `version` parameter is a two-item tuple specifying the macOS version to
 690 │     generate platform tags for. The `arch` parameter is the CPU architecture to
 691 │     generate platform tags for. Both parameters default to the appropriate value
 692 │     for the current system.
 693 │ 
 694 │     :param tuple version: A two-item tuple representing the version of macOS.
 695 │                           Defaults to the current system's version.
 696 │     :param str arch: The CPU architecture. Defaults to the architecture of the
 697 │                      current system, e.g. ``"x86_64"``.
 698 │ 
 699 │     .. note::
 700 │         Equivalent support for the other major platforms is purposefully not
 701 │         provided:
 702 │ 
 703 │         - On Windows, platform compatibility is statically specified
 704 │         - On Linux, code must be run on the system itself to determine
 705 │           compatibility
 706 │ 
 707 │     .. versionadded:: 20.0
 708 │     """
 709 │     if version is None or arch is None:
 710 │         version_str, _, cpu_arch = platform.mac_ver()
 711 │         if version is None:
 712 │             version = cast("AppleVersion", tuple(map(int, version_str.split(".")[:2])))
 713 │             if version == (10, 16):
 714 │                 # When built against an older macOS SDK, Python will report macOS 10.16
 715 │                 # instead of the real version.
 716 │                 version_str = subprocess.run(
 717 │                     [
 718 │                         sys.executable,
 719 │                         "-sS",
 720 │                         "-c",
 721 │                         "import platform; print(platform.mac_ver()[0])",
 722 │                     ],
 723 │                     check=True,
 724 │                     env={"SYSTEM_VERSION_COMPAT": "0"},
 725 │                     stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
 726 │                     text=True,
 727 │                 ).stdout
 728 │                 version = cast(
 729 │                     "AppleVersion", tuple(map(int, version_str.split(".")[:2]))
 730 │                 )
 731 │         if arch is None:
 732 │             arch = _mac_arch(cpu_arch)
 733 │ 
 734 │     if (10, 0) <= version < (11, 0):
 735 │         # Prior to Mac OS 11, each yearly release of Mac OS bumped the
 736 │         # "minor" version number.  The major version was always 10.

 397 │ def cpython_tags(
 398 │     python_version: PythonVersion | None = None,
 399 │     abis: Iterable[str] | None = None,
 400 │     platforms: Iterable[str] | None = None,
 401 │     *,
 402 │     warn: bool = False,
 403 │ ) -> Iterator[Tag]:
 404 │     """
 405 │     Yields the tags for the CPython interpreter.
 406 │ 
 407 │     The specific tags generated are:
 408 │ 
 409 │     - ``cp<python_version>-<abi>-<platform>``
 410 │     - ``cp<python_version>-<stable_abi>-<platform>``
 411 │     - ``cp<python_version>-none-<platform>``
 412 │     - ``cp<older version>-<stable_abi>-<platform>`` where "older version" is all older
 413 │       minor versions down to Python 3.2 (when ``abi3`` was introduced)
 414 │ 
 415 │     If ``python_version`` only provides a major-only version then only
 416 │     user-provided ABIs via ``abis`` and the ``none`` ABI will be used.
 417 │ 
 418 │     The ``stable_abi`` will be either ``abi3`` or ``abi3t`` if `abi` is a
 419 │     GIL-enabled ABI like `"cp315"` or a free-threaded ABI like `"cp315t"`,
 420 │     respectively.
 421 │ 
 422 │     :param Sequence python_version: A one- or two-item sequence representing the
 423 │                                  targeted Python version. Defaults to
 424 │                                  ``sys.version_info[:2]``.
 425 │     :param Iterable abis: Iterable of compatible ABIs. Defaults to the ABIs
 426 │                           compatible with the current system.
 427 │     :param Iterable platforms: Iterable of compatible platforms. Defaults to the
 428 │                                platforms compatible with the current system.
 429 │     :param bool warn: Whether warnings should be logged. Defaults to ``False``.
 430 │ 
 431 │     .. versionadded:: 20.0
 432 │     """
 433 │     if not python_version:
 434 │         python_version = sys.version_info[:2]
 435 │ 
 436 │     interpreter = f"cp{_version_nodot(python_version[:2])}"
 437 │ 
 438 │     if abis is None:
 439 │         abis = _cpython_abis(python_version, warn) if len(python_version) > 1 else []
 440 │     abis = list(abis)
 441 │     threading = _is_threaded_cpython(abis)
 442 │     # Stable ABIs and 'none' are explicitly handled later.
 443 │     explicit_abis = ("abi3", "abi3t", "none") if threading else ("abi3", "none")
 444 │     for explicit_abi in explicit_abis:
 445 │         try:
 446 │             abis.remove(explicit_abi)
 447 │         except ValueError:  # noqa: PERF203
 448 │             pass
 449 │ 
 450 │     platforms = list(platforms or platform_tags())
 451 │     for abi in abis:
 452 │         for platform_ in platforms:
 453 │             yield Tag(interpreter, abi, platform_)
 454 │ 
 455 │     use_abi3 = _abi3_applies(python_version, threading)
 456 │     use_abi3t = _abi3t_applies(python_version, threading)
 457 │     if use_abi3:
 458 │         yield from (Tag(interpreter, "abi3", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 459 │     if use_abi3t:
 460 │         yield from (Tag(interpreter, "abi3t", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 461 │ 
 462 │     yield from (Tag(interpreter, "none", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 463 │ 
 464 │     if use_abi3 or use_abi3t:
 465 │         for minor_version in range(python_version[1] - 1, 1, -1):
 466 │             for platform_ in platforms:
 467 │                 version = _version_nodot((python_version[0], minor_version))
 468 │                 interpreter = f"cp{version}"
 469 │                 if use_abi3:
 470 │                     yield Tag(interpreter, "abi3", platform_)
 471 │                 if use_abi3t:
 472 │                     # Support for abi3t was introduced in Python 3.15, but in
 473 │                     # principle abi3t wheels are possible for older limited API
 474 │                     # versions, so allow things like ("cp37", "abi3t", "platform")
 475 │                     yield Tag(interpreter, "abi3t", platform_)

 478 │ def _generic_abi() -> list[str]:
 479 │     """
 480 │     Return the ABI tag based on EXT_SUFFIX.
 481 │     """
 482 │     # The following are examples of `EXT_SUFFIX`.
 483 │     # We want to keep the parts which are related to the ABI and remove the
 484 │     # parts which are related to the platform:
 485 │     # - linux:   '.cpython-310-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' => cp310
 486 │     # - mac:     '.cpython-310-darwin.so'           => cp310
 487 │     # - win:     '.cp310-win_amd64.pyd'             => cp310
 488 │     # - win:     '.pyd'                             => cp37 (uses _cpython_abis())
 489 │     # - pypy:    '.pypy38-pp73-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' => pypy38_pp73
 490 │     # - graalpy: '.graalpy-38-native-x86_64-darwin.dylib'
 491 │     #                                               => graalpy_38_native
 492 │ 
 493 │     ext_suffix = _get_config_var("EXT_SUFFIX", warn=True)
 494 │     if not isinstance(ext_suffix, str) or not ext_suffix.startswith("."):
 495 │         raise SystemError("invalid sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')")
 496 │     parts = ext_suffix.split(".")
 497 │     if len(parts) < 3:
 498 │         # CPython3.7 and earlier uses ".pyd" on Windows.
 499 │         return _cpython_abis(sys.version_info[:2])
 500 │     soabi = parts[1]
 501 │     if soabi.startswith("cpython"):
 502 │         # non-windows
 503 │         cpython_parts = soabi.split("-")
 504 │         if len(cpython_parts) < 2 or not cpython_parts[1]:
 505 │             raise SystemError("invalid sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')")
 506 │         abi = "cp" + cpython_parts[1]
 507 │     elif soabi.startswith("cp"):
 508 │         # windows
 509 │         abi = soabi.split("-")[0]
 510 │     elif soabi.startswith("pypy"):
 511 │         abi = "-".join(soabi.split("-")[:2])
 512 │     elif soabi.startswith("graalpy"):
 513 │         abi = "-".join(soabi.split("-")[:3])
 514 │     elif soabi:
 515 │         # pyston, ironpython, others?
 516 │         abi = soabi
 517 │     else:
 518 │         return []
 519 │     return [_normalize_string(abi)]

 659 │ def mac_platforms(
 660 │     version: AppleVersion | None = None, arch: str | None = None
 661 │ ) -> Iterator[str]:
 662 │     """
 663 │     Yields the :attr:`~Tag.platform` tags for macOS.
 664 │ 
 665 │     The `version` parameter is a two-item tuple specifying the macOS version to
 666 │     generate platform tags for. The `arch` parameter is the CPU architecture to
 667 │     generate platform tags for. Both parameters default to the appropriate value
 668 │     for the current system.
 669 │ 
 670 │     :param tuple version: A two-item tuple representing the version of macOS.
 671 │                           Defaults to the current system's version.
 672 │     :param str arch: The CPU architecture. Defaults to the architecture of the
 673 │                      current system, e.g. ``"x86_64"``.
 674 │ 
 675 │     .. note::
 676 │         Equivalent support for the other major platforms is purposefully not
 677 │         provided:
 678 │ 
 679 │         - On Windows, platform compatibility is statically specified
 680 │         - On Linux, code must be run on the system itself to determine
 681 │           compatibility
 682 │ 
 683 │     .. versionadded:: 20.0
 684 │     """
 685 │     if version is None or arch is None:
 686 │         version_str, _, cpu_arch = platform.mac_ver()
 687 │         if version is None:
 688 │             version = cast("AppleVersion", tuple(map(int, version_str.split(".")[:2])))
 689 │             if version == (10, 16):
 690 │                 # When built against an older macOS SDK, Python will report macOS 10.16
 691 │                 # instead of the real version.
 692 │                 version_str = subprocess.run(
 693 │                     [
 694 │                         sys.executable,
 695 │                         "-sS",
 696 │                         "-c",
 697 │                         "import platform; print(platform.mac_ver()[0])",
 698 │                     ],
 699 │                     check=True,
 700 │                     env={"SYSTEM_VERSION_COMPAT": "0"},
 701 │                     stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
 702 │                     text=True,
 703 │                 ).stdout
 704 │                 version = cast(
 705 │                     "AppleVersion", tuple(map(int, version_str.split(".")[:2]))
 706 │                 )
 707 │         if arch is None:
 708 │             arch = _mac_arch(cpu_arch)
 709 │ 
 710 │     if (10, 0) <= version < (11, 0):
 711 │         # Prior to Mac OS 11, each yearly release of Mac OS bumped the
 712 │         # "minor" version number.  The major version was always 10.
 713 │         major_version = 10
 714 │         for minor_version in range(version[1], -1, -1):
 715 │             compat_version = major_version, minor_version
 716 │             binary_formats = _mac_binary_formats(compat_version, arch)
 717 │             for binary_format in binary_formats:
 718 │                 yield f"macosx_{major_version}_{minor_version}_{binary_format}"
 719 │ 
 720 │     if version >= (11, 0):
 721 │         # Starting with Mac OS 11, each yearly release bumps the major version
 722 │         # number.   The minor versions are now the midyear updates.
 723 │         minor_version = 0
 724 │         for major_version in range(version[0], 10, -1):
 725 │             compat_version = major_version, minor_version
 726 │             binary_formats = _mac_binary_formats(compat_version, arch)
 727 │             for binary_format in binary_formats:
 728 │                 yield f"macosx_{major_version}_{minor_version}_{binary_format}"
 729 │ 
 730 │         # Mac OS 11 on x86_64 is compatible with binaries from previous releases.
 731 │         # Arm64 support was introduced in 11.0, so no Arm binaries from previous
 732 │         # releases exist.
 733 │         #
 734 │         # However, the "universal2" binary format can have a
 735 │         # macOS version earlier than 11.0 when the x86_64 part of the binary supports
 736 │         # that version of macOS.
 737 │         major_version = 10
 738 │         if arch == "x86_64":
 739 │             for minor_version in range(16, 3, -1):
 740 │                 compat_version = major_version, minor_version
 741 │                 binary_formats = _mac_binary_formats(compat_version, arch)
 742 │                 for binary_format in binary_formats:
 743 │                     yield f"macosx_{major_version}_{minor_version}_{binary_format}"
 744 │         else:
 745 │             for minor_version in range(16, 3, -1):
 746 │                 compat_version = major_version, minor_version
 747 │                 binary_format = "universal2"
 748 │                 yield f"macosx_{major_version}_{minor_version}_{binary_format}"

 751 │ def ios_platforms(
 752 │     version: AppleVersion | None = None, multiarch: str | None = None
 753 │ ) -> Iterator[str]:
 754 │     """
 755 │ 
 756 │     Yields the :attr:`~Tag.platform` tags for iOS.
 757 │ 
 758 │     :param tuple version: A two-item tuple representing the version of iOS.
 759 │                           Defaults to the current system's version.
 760 │     :param str multiarch: The CPU architecture+ABI to be used. This should be in
 761 │                           the format by ``sys.implementation._multiarch`` (e.g.,
 762 │                           ``arm64_iphoneos`` or ``x86_64_iphonesimulator``).
 763 │                           Defaults to the current system's multiarch value.
 764 │ 
 765 │     .. note::
 766 │         Behavior of this method is undefined if invoked on non-iOS platforms
 767 │         without providing explicit version and multiarch arguments.
 768 │ 
 769 │     .. versionadded:: 24.2
 770 │     """
 771 │     if version is None:
 772 │         # if iOS is the current platform, ios_ver *must* be defined. However,
 773 │         # it won't exist for CPython versions before 3.13, which causes a mypy
 774 │         # error.
 775 │         _, release, _, _ = platform.ios_ver()  # type: ignore[attr-defined, unused-ignore]
 776 │         version = cast("AppleVersion", tuple(map(int, release.split(".")[:2])))
 777 │ 
 778 │     if multiarch is None:
 779 │         multiarch = sys.implementation._multiarch
 780 │     multiarch = multiarch.replace("-", "_")
 781 │ 
 782 │     ios_platform_template = "ios_{major}_{minor}_{multiarch}"
 783 │ 
 784 │     # Consider any iOS major.minor version from the version requested, down to
 785 │     # 12.0. 12.0 is the first iOS version that is known to have enough features
 786 │     # to support CPython. Consider every possible minor release up to X.9. There
 787 │     # highest the minor has ever gone is 8 (14.8 and 15.8) but having some extra
 788 │     # candidates that won't ever match doesn't really hurt, and it saves us from
 789 │     # having to keep an explicit list of known iOS versions in the code. Return
 790 │     # the results descending order of version number.
 791 │ 
 792 │     # If the requested major version is less than 12, there won't be any matches.
 793 │     if version[0] < 12:
 794 │         return
 795 │ 
 796 │     # Consider the actual X.Y version that was requested.
 797 │     yield ios_platform_template.format(
 798 │         major=version[0], minor=version[1], multiarch=multiarch
 799 │     )
 800 │ 
 801 │     # Consider every minor version from X.0 to the minor version prior to the
 802 │     # version requested by the platform.
 803 │     for minor in range(version[1] - 1, -1, -1):
 804 │         yield ios_platform_template.format(
 805 │             major=version[0], minor=minor, multiarch=multiarch
 806 │         )
 807 │ 
 808 │     for major in range(version[0] - 1, 11, -1):
 809 │         for minor in range(9, -1, -1):
 810 │             yield ios_platform_template.format(
 811 │                 major=major, minor=minor, multiarch=multiarch
 812 │             )
